cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, has just counted every man twenty and older who can serve in the army (Numbers 1:2-3). That's a LOT of people, friend. Now the LORD speaks to Moses and his brother Aaron (Exodus 4:14), and the big question is: where do you PUT everybody?

cards.question: The LORD tells the Israelites to camp all the way around something. What sits at the center of it all?
True or false: the LORD tells the tribes to pitch their tents right up against the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: They camp at a distance, each man under his standard, with the banners of his family. It's like the giant signs in a parking garage, so nobody's wandering around at night going, "Wait, were we in Section B?"

cards.question: The LORD starts with the east side of the camp, toward the sunrise. Which tribe's divisions camp there?

cards.text: Judah's leader is Nahshon son of Amminadab, and his division alone is 74,600 men. Issachar and Zebulun camp right next to them, so the east side is PACKED like a cookie box on a holiday.

cards.question: The camp of Judah has 186,400 men in all. When Israel moves, the LORD says they shall set out ___.

cards.text: South side: the camp of Reuben, led by Elizur son of Shedeur, with Simeon and Gad beside them. That's 151,450 men setting out second, and second is FINE, friend, I spent years at the back of a drawer.
East and south are set, but before the LORD gets to the other two sides, He talks about the middle. That's the part everybody's camped around.

cards.question: When Israel is on the move, who travels with the Tent of Meeting in the middle of the camps?
True or false: when they set out, each tribe travels in the same order it camped, in its own place under its standard.

cards.text: West side: the camp of Ephraim, led by Elishama son of Ammihud, with Manasseh and Benjamin beside them. That's 108,100 men setting out third, and I have officially run out of mustache to count on.
Three sides down, one to go. Somebody's getting that last spot, and I'm staring at it like it's the last cookie on the tray.

cards.question: East, south and west are all taken. Which side of the camp is left for the last group of tribes?

cards.text: On the north side camps Dan, led by Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, with Asher and Naphtali beside them. That's 157,600 men setting out LAST, and hey, somebody's gotta turn off the oven on the way out.

cards.question: True or false: with the camp of Dan setting out last, the Tent of Meeting travels at the very back, right behind them.

cards.text: Add it all up and you get 603,550 men, more than SIX HUNDRED THOUSAND. Friend, I've packed a LOT of cookie boxes in my bakery, and I have never once counted that high.

cards.question: True or false: the Levites, who travel with the Tent of Meeting, are counted in that total of 603,550.
So how do the Israelites handle the LORD's plan for camping and setting out?

answers.text: They follow only part of it
They swap a few of the spots

findings.problem: The repeated tribal camp reports in Numbers 2:3-16 and Numbers 2:18-31 are census-style, detail-heavy repeated reports. Cards 5, 7 and 14 nevertheless quiz details from those reports instead of leaving the material to summary story cards.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on predicting an unseen detail rather than reasoning from earlier cards. Cards 3, 5, 7, 10 and 19 are clear discovery guesses, and card 11 also has no setup pointing toward its answer. Even if every other choice were treated as informed, informed guesses would make up at most half of the stop, not most of it.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank simply asks for the unseen word completing verse 9's statement about setting out. Nothing earlier establishes Judah's marching position, so the baker is guessing wording rather than reasoning out meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "Out past the east side" is an invented location, not a real detail from somewhere in the Bible, even though this is a which-side/where question.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
